What will carpet installation cost me in Kirkland, WA?

Figure $4 to $7 per square foot installed in Kirkland — that covers carpet, pad, labor, new tack strip and haul-away. Typical projects come in between $2,000 and $4,500, while 1,200 sq ft of bedrooms and hallway plus a staircase usually totals $5,500 to $8,500. The grade of carpet you pick swings the price more than anything else, and you pick it from samples laid out in your own home.
Does the mobile carpet showroom come to Kirkland?

It does — Kirkland is home turf for us. The van carries 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades to your house or condo, we set the samples down in the rooms being carpeted so the color reads true in your own daylight, then measure everything and write up your price during the same stop. The visit costs nothing and there's no store trip involved.
What does carpet stretching run in Kirkland?

Stretching starts at $99 per room in Kirkland. A power stretcher pulls the ripples, waves and bunching out of carpet that still has life in it, at roughly a fifth of what new carpet would cost — the sensible fix when the pile stands up and the color still works for you.
What do carpeted stairs cost in Kirkland?

Stair installation starts at $18 per step, done waterfall or cap-and-band, whichever suits your staircase. Kirkland's two-story and split-entry homes often have landings and pie-shaped winders — those go into the written quote from the start instead of showing up as an extra charge afterward.
How long will my Kirkland carpet install take?

One day, for most Kirkland homes. A typical upstairs — three or four bedrooms and a staircase — is a routine single day for the crew. A full house with heavy furniture or lots of stairs can stretch into a second day, and if it will, the timeline is written on your quote so there are no surprises.
Will the installers move my furniture?

Yes — moving beds, dressers, couches and tables is part of the job on most installs, and everything goes back where it stood. What we ask of you: empty the closets and clear small items, electronics and anything fragile or personal you'd rather handle yourself.
Is restretching my carpet worth it, or should I replace?

Restretch when the pile still stands, the backing is sound and the color still suits the room — at $99 per room it's a fraction of replacement. Replace when traffic lanes are crushed flat, seams are letting go, the backing is breaking down, or pet odor has outlasted professional cleaning. We inspect and tell you honestly which side of the line yours is on before quoting.
What parts of Kirkland do you cover?

All of them — Moss Bay, Market, Norkirk, Highlands, Everest, Lakeview, Central Houghton, Bridle Trails, North and South Rose Hill, Kingsgate, Totem Lake, Juanita and Finn Hill, plus the condos downtown and at Carillon Point. Beyond Kirkland we cover the rest of the Eastside and Seattle.
Which carpet holds up best with pets?

Solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing, laid over a moisture-barrier pad. The sealed backing and the barrier pad keep accidents from soaking into the subfloor — the real source of permanent odor — and solution-dyed fiber tolerates cleaning with diluted bleach without fading. The barrier pad upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot, and we bring pet-focused samples to every Kirkland visit.
What warranty do I get on the installation?

OC Flooring backs the workmanship with a 1-year warranty, and the carpet itself carries the mill's warranty — commonly 10 to 25 years against wear and staining depending on the grade. Both appear in writing on your quote. One catch worth knowing: some mill warranties require a minimum pad grade, which is one more reason all three grades come to the measure.
